summary: Harogadde Manappa Nayak worked in linguistics, Indology, and other fields. He served as Director at the University of Mysore (~1961–1991) and Vice-chancellor at Gulbarga University (1984–1987), and he taught T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

Harold G. Coward is a scholar in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his doctorate at McMaster University (~1969–1973). He held posts at the University of Calgary (~1974–1992), its Press (1981–1983), and the University of Victoria (~1992–2002).

Harold Hargreaves worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a headmaster in Amritsar and held multiple posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, including Superintendent (1914), Frontier Circle Superintendent (~1914–1931), and Deputy Director General (1928–1931).

Harold Scheub earned degrees at the University of Michigan, UCLA, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD ~1966–1969). After teaching at Valparaiso University and Masindi Senior Secondary School, he was Evjue-Bascom Professor of Humanities Emeritus at Wisconsin-Madison (~1970–2013).
Harold Stewart was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied at the University of Sydney and the Sydney Conservatorium of Music.

Harold Walter Bailey specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Western Australia and Oxford under F. W. Thomas. He taught at SOAS (1929) and held the Sanskrit chair at Cambridge (1936–1967).

Haroon Khan Sherwani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Aligarh Muslim University, Oxford, and under Ghulam Yazdani. He held positions at Osmania University (~1919–1945), Nizam College (~1945–1948), and Zakir Husain Delhi College (~1948–1951).
Harry Falk is a scholar of Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Gaya Charan Tripathi. He served as Director at the Free University of Berlin from 1993 to 2012.
Hartmut Buescher works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, having studied under Chandrabhal Tripathi. He has held appointments at the University of Copenhagen and the Royal Danish Library.
Hartmut Scharfe was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctoral studies under Paul Thieme and held a academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Hartmut-Ortwin Feistel worked in Indology. He served as head at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1989) and held posts in the Oriental Department of the Prussian State Library (attested 1982, 1992–1994).

Haruhiko Masaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Gakushuin University and the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Nagasaki University (attested 1988) and founded the Japan Association for Bioethics in 1988.
Haruka Yanagisawa was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1988–2007) and Chiba University (attested 2005).

Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed both her MA (-1994) and PhD (-2001) at the University of California, Los Angeles, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert Buswell.

Harunaga Isaacson specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, having studied at Groningen and Leiden. He has held positions at Oxford, Groningen, the University of Pennsylvania (2002–2006), and the University of Hamburg (Professor since 2006).

Harushige Kōzu was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Tokyo (1938–1948) and later served as professor and dean at Musashi University (1968).

Harvey B. Aronson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson, was a professor at the University of Virginia (attested 1988), and served as co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism (attested 2001).

Haya Akegarasu was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University. He later served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji (~1951–1954) and as chief administrator of Shinshu Otani-ha (1951–1952).

Heather Stoddard is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1967–1970) with D. C. Lau and also studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas.

Heeraman Tiwari is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Lucknow, Delhi, and Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~2001), Heidelberg (2011–2012), and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (2014–2015).
